item.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
item.description:
Skim new method — Generalizes pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution to state-dependent operations without approximation. Reaches up to 24× higher throughput than CUDA-Q on distance-3 topological memories with amplitude damping, and up to 83× higher throughput on 30-qubit random circuits with mid-circuit measurements.

Grade 0.583 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Validating quantum computers using randomized model circuits” · Louis Follet, Paavai Pari, Isidor Schoch, Thien Nguyen, Justin G. Lietz, Daniel Lowell, Brucek Khailany, Krysta M. Svore, Dirk R. Englund, Taylor L. Patti

Figure

Throughput speedup of generalized PTSBE over CUDA-Q and Clifft as a function of non-Clifford gate fraction and total shots across surface codes, color codes, and 16-to-30-qubit random circuits.

Asks

Can pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution be extended to circuits with mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels without approximation?

Before

Original PTSBE required stochastic outcomes to be state-independent (mixtures of unitaries), excluding mid-circuit measurements and non-twirled amplitude damping.

But

Single-precision statevectors; limited by GPU memory for caching intermediate state branches (requires 8⋅2n bytes per cached state, e.g., 8 GiB per state at n=30 qubits).

Tools

generalized pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) · delayed inner product algorithm · GPU statevector simulator (CUDA-Q extension) · multinomial branching and cached state reuse

Abstract

Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. Each event is partially pre-sampled, while deferred outcomes are drawn during grouped execution via multinomial branching and cached-state reuse. We implement the method for GPUs as an extension of CUDA-Q. On distance-3 topological code memories under amplitude damping, it is up to 24x faster than conventional trajectory sampling in CUDA-Q. On 30-qubit random circuits with mid-circuit measurements, it is up to 83x faster and outperforms the near-Clifford simulator Clifft when more than about 25% of the gates are non-Clifford. With repeated sampling of each final state, its sampling rate per trajectory exceeds that of CUDA-Q by nearly five orders of magnitude. Our method also allows us to compare exact amplitude damping with its Pauli-twirled channel on a surface-code memory, revealing that twirling overestimates the detection rate by 21% and raises the logical error rate of a lookup decoder by 8%. This work makes exact, high-throughput simulation practical for general noisy circuits, from data generation for training decoders to studying measurement-based fault-tolerant protocols under realistic noise.

arxave:action.title: Evaluate PTSBE for spin-qubit noise-model validation

item.arxave:action: Use the generalized PTSBE method to generate exact amplitude-damping/Kraus trajectories for the spin-qubit QEC and decoder pipeline, and compare against Pauli-twirling approximations to see whether the reported twirling bias affects decoder-training assumptions.

arxave:action.title: Prototype CUDA-Q PTSBE extension in simulation workflow

item.arxave:action: Integrate the CUDA-Q GPU extension into the team's noisy-circuit sampling and benchmarking workflow for QEC decoder data generation, measuring throughput and memory use on the HPC cluster.
